# Preregistration: auto-generated glossaries

Written before any glossary was generated for the servers below, and before any
model run on their tasks.

## What is tested

The glossary arm with a command table **generated by a model from the server's
`listTools()` output**, run by the generic engine (`src/auto/engine.ts`), with
no hand edits. Generation is one shot plus at most 2 automated repair rounds
driven by the static validator (`src/auto/validate.ts`); every round is logged.

Servers:

- `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem@2.0.0` (14 tools) - never used before
  in this study. Tasks: `src/fs/tasks.ts` (10), seed `src/fs/seed.ts`.
- `mcp-server-git` 2026.10.19 via uvx (12 tools) - never used before in this
  study. Tasks: `src/git/tasks.ts` (10), seed `src/git/seed.ts`.
- `github-mcp-server` v2.0.3, default toolsets (46 tools) and all toolsets
  (91 tools), on the existing 12 GitHub tasks. For 91 tools, the 45 extra tools
  are distractors: the tasks and the fake backend use only default-toolset routes.

Arms: native, glossary (auto table), code (Cloudflare style), on the same server.
For GitHub, the auto table is also compared against the hand-written one.

## Prediction

1. Auto-glossary accuracy is within noise of native on every model.
2. Auto-glossary tool definitions are at least 2x smaller than native.
3. On GitHub, the auto table performs within noise of the hand-written table.

## What refutes it

- The auto-glossary arm loses 3 or more task-runs (out of 3 reps x 10 tasks)
  on a model where native does not, on either new server.
- Or its definitions are less than 2x smaller than native.
- Or the generator cannot produce a table that passes the validator within 2
  repair rounds (then the method is not automatic for that server).

With 3 reps, a difference of 1 or 2 task-runs is not claimed as a difference.

## Freeze

Task and seed files are hashed in `results/auto-freeze.sha256` before generation.
Generated tables are hashed right after generation and never edited by hand.
